input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months, but the non-renewal notice window is 180 days — beyond the fallback maximum of 60 days and within walk-away territory (windows longer than 90 days). The pricing limb already beats our position: § 8.3 caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and three percent. We therefore target the fallback level and make the single smallest change, shortening the window to sixty (60) days (numeral included for clarity); the renewal term is already twelve months and no Vendor reminder mechanic exists (a preferred-only sub-element noted but not flagged).

proposal.summary: Shorten the Order Form non-renewal notice window from 180 to sixty (60) days
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window in § 8.2 from one hundred eighty days to sixty (60) days, which is our fallback maximum; a 180-day window is in walk-away territory. The CPI/3% uplift cap in § 8.3 already satisfies our pricing position, so no other change is needed.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent.
